chapter: Forming the band in New York
title: Shaping the band's sound and swing tempo
summary: Arrangements from Sam Lowe, Bill Johnson and others, a chosen swing tempo and Hawkins's high notes formed the sound.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, it's beginning to appear more and more that you began to emerge as the band leader because you were the one who was able to do everything. I mean, that you were, you had a particular focus. Did you have a sound in mind for the band? I mean, did you have a specific way that you thought it should sound?

As the arrangements came in, we took it from there. More arrangements from Sam. I had another fellow there by the name of Bill Johnson, first alto. He came in later. He was arranger. William McLamore, he came in later. And then we, after that, after I got all these arranged together, then I used to sit with them and we'd talk it over. And then, I'd use just a certain swing, certain tempo I wanted, I liked, in that swing tempo. Then, once we got into that, then the sound came a little later. They started Bill and me in between with those high notes mostly. Dud was
doing the, you know, regular solos now that I was leading.
